newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Exchange rate hits Donaghys in 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Exchange rate hits Donaghys in 2nd half.

text.p: New Zealand manufacturer Donaghys Ltd said on Friday its second half profit was affected by the impact of the higher exchange rate and lower economic activity in New Zealand and Australia.
The performance was also reduced by the effect of the lower capital base after repayment of $30.5 million of the company's cash reserves to shareholders.
However, a higher level of manufacturing output and customer demand since balance date reflected increased business confidence.
The company reported a June year net profit of NZ$5.5 million against $29.6 million previously.
Donaghys said it was responding to challenging conditions by a further rationalisation of facilities.

It said it would benefit from its investment of more than $10 million in major plant installations over the last two years and this year's record operating cashflow surplus of $18.1 million reflected the strong financial structure of the group.
Operating results for Donaghys Industries cordage and textile operations during the second half of the financial year were below forecast.
The restructuring programme will mean the relocation during the next year of the Auckland operations to alternative premises following the conditional sale of the company's Glendene property.
Donaghy's has also undertaken a rationalisation of its Melbourne manufacturing division to focus on a range of products with sustainable competitive advantage in the Australian market.
Donaghy's makes cordage textiles, webbings and braids, electronics, rural products and plastic packaging.
